extraction.paper_title: Fuzzy-Based Thermal Management Scheme for 3D Chip Multicores with Stacked Caches

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 6(a)/(b): transient maximum temperature, mem2 and com2 program sets (with Section 4 setup on PDF pages 8-9)
scenario.description: Transient maximum temperature curves, 200-450 ms, comparing Baseline (DVFS), FLC (fuzzy control only) and FBTM (fuzzy control plus dynamic cache reconfiguration) while executing the mem2 and com2 multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 workload sets. The paper reports about 3 degrees C reduction and fluctuation within 0.5 degrees for FLC/FBTM versus up to 3.5 degrees for the baseline. No block coordinates, dimensions or per-block powers are published, so no floorplan can be extracted.
scenario.architecture: 3D-stacked NUCA cache: 4 cores in one core layer nearest the heat sink, with 3 stacked L2 cache layers. Each cache layer has 16 banks of 256 KB (CACTI), grouped into 4 cache zones of 4 banks, each zone sitting above one core. Each core has 32KB L1I and 32KB L1D. TSV-connected.
scenario.workload: Multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 sets of four applications each; Figure 6 shows mem2 (libquantum, lbm, GemsFDTD, art) and com2 (hmmer, mpeg_dec, astar). Power traces generated by gem5 and McPAT.
scenario.operating_point: Runtime-varying thermal threshold (per ref. 19); control step intervals; Algorithm 1 interval T = 2M clock cycles, allowed cache miss-rate degradation 3%; maximum temperature plotted roughly 75-81 degrees C over 200-450 ms. Ambient temperature, Vdd and frequency values are not given.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot grid-based thermal simulation, driven by gem5 (with Ruby memory model) performance traces and McPAT power traces. Cache bank capacity from CACTI. Super-core compact thermal model adapted from Zhou et al. (ref 9), Eqs. 1-2, PDF page 3.
original_setup.optimizer: No numerical optimizer. Dynamic cache reconfiguration (Algorithm 1) greedily gates cache banks, farthest from the heat sink first, using shadow-tag miss-rate prediction. Interval T = 2M clock cycles, allowed miss-rate degradation 3%.
original_setup.controller: Per-super-core fuzzy logic controller (FBTM). Inputs are the error e(n) between threshold and measured temperature (range [0,3]) and the temperature change rate (range [-1.5,1.5]). Each input has 3 triangular membership functions. 9 rules, mean-of-maxima defuzzification. Output is a normalized frequency ratio. FLC is the same controller without cache reconfiguration. Baseline is the DVFS technique of ref 18. Threshold is runtime-varying (ref 19).
original_setup.benchmark: Multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 workload sets of four applications each (com1, com2, med1, med2, mem1, mem2; Table 3, PDF page 9). Selected scenario is Figure 6 (PDF page 10): transient maximum temperature for mem2 and com2, 200-450 ms, comparing Baseline, FLC and FBTM.

thermal_observable.location: Transient maximum chip temperature over time (Figure 6a/b, mem2 and com2 sets). The plotted axis spans roughly 75-81 degC. The text reports about 3 degC reduction for FLC/FBTM versus baseline, with fluctuation within 0.5 degC versus up to 3.5 degC for the baseline. Exact per-curve numeric values are not tabulated.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the chip per control step, plotted as a time series over 200-450 ms. The 3 degC reduction is described as an average across the experiments (abstract). No single scalar is published for the selected scenario.

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D stacked architecture: one core layer plus three stacked L2 cache layers connected by TSVs, with a vertical super-core thermal model. A steady-state 2D single-layer floorplan cannot represent the inter-layer vertical coupling or the per-layer cache power gating.

Transient and controller-in-the-loop observable: the temperature trace depends on closed-loop fuzzy DVFS and runtime cache bank gating (a runtime-varying threshold). A static thermal solve cannot reproduce it.

No block geometry (x, y, width, height) or per-block power values are published. The paper gives only qualitative layout (Figure 1) and no per-block watts, so no complete floorplan or power set exists for this scenario.

Solver mismatch: the original uses HotSpot grid mode with gem5/McPAT power traces and the compact super-core model of Eqs. 1-2. The Studio solver is not the same toolchain, and the thermal resistances (Ramb, Rv), ambient temperature and package are not given.
Cooling and package parameters (heat sink, TIM, layer thicknesses, interposer or bonding layers) are not specified. Only the heat sink proximity of the core layer is stated.

findings.reason: The extraction sets kind='custom_2d_steady' with an empty floorplan and empty power_w. This contradicts its own steady_2d_relevant=false and the essential physical_mismatches (3D stack, transient closed-loop DVFS and cache gating). It labels a non-reproducible 3D transient scenario as a 2D steady experiment. It should be marked not extractable or not applicable.

The provenance says 'Digitized axis range from figure text extraction'. No figure image was supplied, only pdftotext tick labels. The decisive Figure 6 was therefore not visually verified. The curves, the 75-81 degC span, and the claimed ordering of Baseline, FLC and FBTM are unconfirmed from the evidence.

The claim that Figure 1 has no coordinates or dimensions and that no power table exists rests on text extraction only. Figure 1 and the other figure images were not visually inspected. The absence of geometry is plausible but not visually verified. Per-block power is confirmed absent only in the text.

The units of e(n) (degC) and of the rate (degC per step) are presumed, not stated. The Figure 5 membership points (0, 1.5, 3 and -1.5, 0, 1.5) come from extracted text labels, not an inspected figure image. The output membership parameters (0.25, 0.5, 0.75) are not extracted as parameters.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed false). The selected scenario is Figure 6(a)/(b) of W3006943355: transient maximum temperature, 200-450 ms, for the mem2 and com2 workload sets under Baseline DVFS, FLC and FBTM. It comes from a 3D-stacked system with 4 cores, 3 TSV-connected L2 cache layers, closed-loop fuzzy DVFS and dynamic cache bank gating, simulated with HotSpot, gem5 and McPAT. The extracted experiment is a custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and no power_w, so the input gate failed (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). The scientific gate also failed. Many evidence items lack a valid page or pinned asset locator, no cited steady/transient regime or paper thermal observable was recorded, the adversarial checks are unresolved, and independent review is pending. No Studio temperature exists, so comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison is made. A custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace in any case. The paper's only quantitative statements are approximate and text-based: about 3 degC average reduction for FLC/FBTM versus baseline, fluctuation within 0.5 degC versus up to 3.5 degC for the baseline, and a plotted axis of roughly 75-81 degC. These are not per-scenario scalars and cannot be matched to any 2D steady quantity. Qualitatively, the paper suggests that active temperature control and cache gating can reduce peak temperature and its variation in 3D stacks, but this run neither confirms nor refutes that claim. The result is a screening outcome only, not a replication.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated result to compare against the paper.
The extracted experiment has no floorplan blocks and no per-block power; geometry and watts are not published, and total chip power must not be split without a published rule.
The paper scenario is a 3D stack (1 core layer plus 3 cache layers, TSVs, vertical super-core model) that a single-layer 2D steady model cannot represent.
The observable is a transient, controller-in-the-loop maximum temperature trace with a runtime-varying threshold, whereas a custom 2D steady run yields no transient trace.
Solver and toolchain mismatch: the paper uses HotSpot grid mode with gem5/McPAT power traces and a compact super-core model, with no published configuration.
Ambient temperature, Vdd, frequency levels, thermal resistances (Ramb, Rv), heat sink, TIM, layer thicknesses and package are all unspecified.

No numeric curve values are published for Figure 6; only approximate text statements (about 3 degC average reduction, 0.5 vs 3.5 degC fluctuation). Digitizing the curves would add substantial uncertainty, and the 3 degC figure is an average across experiments, not a value for this scenario.
No paper-linked assets, code, configs or data were found (checked_no_links), and the com2 workload lists only three applications while the text describes four.
Feasibility gate failures include missing page/asset locators on the evidence items, no cited thermal observable or regime, unresolved adversarial checks and pending independent review.
Because the gate controls the verdict, the final verdict is not_2d_applicable with comparison_valid false; no exact replication or numerical agreement is claimed.
